evidence.snippet: - TSDoc only on exported package API. Nothing on internals.

verification.reason: AGENTS.md line 33 says "TSDoc only on exported package API. Nothing on internals." and packages/core/AGENTS.md line 13 says only what src/index.ts exports carries TSDoc. SwitchOff is exported from analyser.ts, but index.ts exports only parseJsonc from that file (line 21). Only guardrails.ts and the file's own code use the type. The type is new at head, since base has no SwitchOff. The block at lines 99-102 therefore breaks the rule. This is the same P3 advisory the repo has fixed many times before. The failure scenario is thin, but the rule violation is real.

I traced both cases in the code. `SightingBudget.fit` sizes the local findings with `finding.toJSON()` (sighting-budget.ts:51-60) and `runCheck` applies it at checks.ts:323-328. The exported record is built differently. `sighting()` (review-records.ts:430-440) rewrites every `static.*` finding to fixed sentences, so the budget's measure and the exported record's size differ.

Case 1, Biome and tsc: static.ts:419 already makes the local text the fixed sentence. The export `what` adds a `${check} reports ${rule} here. ${withheld}.` sentence and uses `withheld` for `whyHere` and `whatToDo`. That makes it longer than the local text, which the head's own decision file counts as 518 bytes against 487. A check whose local findings sit just under the 4,190,208-byte budget therefore passes `fit` and the verdict is stored. The export then exceeds `recordLimit` and `storable()` throws (record.ts:327-330), which is a store error with exit code 2. The window is narrow, about 6% of the limit.

Case 2, Enola and mutation: `fit` measures the tool-written message text, so it can throw `recordTooLarge` for a check whose exported record, with that text replaced by `withheld`, would fit. The review then reads not reviewed. The base had no budget, so this one is a regression.

No guard stops either case. The head decision file (docs/decisions/2026-11-20-guardrails-record-fits-the-store.md:38-44) lists both under "Known limits" and defers them to issue #626. That file is head-only and is the thing under review, so it doesn't excuse them. Neither case lets a blocking verdict pass, so it fails closed or errors loudly, which is why I left the severity at P2.
